tool_input.command:
git -C <repo> commit -q -m "fix(mission): correct the truncation scope and close its bypasses

Review round on PR #517. Six findings, four real.

The contract scope named delegations[].message, which is not a field
of DelegationTemplate — KnownFields rejects that key before the walk
ever runs, so it guarded nothing — while preconditions[].message, the
gate-denial string a blocked worker is shown, went unguarded. Both
corrected, and TestEveryScopedFieldExistsAndIsChecked now resolves
every scope entry against the Go type by reflection and then probes it
through the real decoder, so a path that names a field the schema does
not have cannot pass. Re-introducing the defect fails it with 'step 2:
mission.DelegationTemplate has no yaml field \"message\"'. The
reflection half is load-bearing: Inputs has a custom UnmarshalYAML
that decodes its subtree without KnownFields, so a typo under
inputs.trigger would otherwise parse, be walked, and report a
truncation for a field that does not exist.

Paths were wrongly treated as constrained. validateWriteSetEntry
rejects null bytes, colons, drive letters, and traversal but not
spaces, so `path: reports/PR #515.txt` landed as `reports/PR` and
could still satisfy write-set containment — persisting a different
file than the worker declared. The rule is now stated in terms of the
property that decides it: a field is checked when its grammar admits
whitespace. That covers free text and paths, and excludes handles,
enums, mission IDs, timestamps, and numbers, which is why the
scaffolds' trailing comments on those fields still pass. The scaffolds
now quote their two path values.

YAML aliases and merge keys bypassed the check entirely: decoding
resolves indirection, so a scalar anchored on `author` and truncated
at its '#' arrived at evidence[0].name as an alias node with no value
to inspect. Verified reachable, then refused outright rather than
resolved — a mission artifact is an audit record, one needing alias
resolution to read is a poor one, and a resolver subtly wrong about
nested merges would reopen the bypass while looking closed. An anchor
nothing refers to stays legal.

The CHANGELOG advertised the field that did not exist. Rewritten to
list actual coverage per command. An entry that overstates what a
guard protects is the defect this PR exists to close.

The message no longer asserts truncation. `path/to/file.go   # note`
loses nothing, so calling it truncated was false — it now reports
where YAML ended the value, what it kept, what it dropped, and offers
both remedies without deciding which the author meant.

cmd test no longer skips its assertions when LoadResult errors.
LoadResult returns (nil, nil) for an absent result and propagates
every real failure, so the load is now required to succeed before
asserting absence.

Not reproducible, evidence in the report: qodo's claim that
`prose: # no narrative` is rejected as truncated. yaml.v3 attaches a
valueless key's trailing comment to the KEY node and leaves the value
node !!null with no comment; the check reads value nodes. Verified
across four empty-value shapes. Two tests added to keep it that way.

29 ok, 0 FAIL with -race."
